cohort: The study analyzed 81,913 infants born at 33-36 weeks gestational age from 2007 to 2008 using the Nationwide Inpatient Sample Database.
finding: Gestational age, birth weight, gender, mode of delivery, multiple gestation, birth region, and primary insurance payer significantly affect the length of hospital stay in late preterm infants, with these variables being more critical for infants born at 35-36 weeks.
mod_finding: Delivery via C-section was significantly associated with an increased risk of a length of hospital stay greater than 3 days (RR=1.46; CI: 1.41-1.51).
birth_weight: Measured as a factor; specifically, <2500g was associated with longer LOS.
